title: Onboard Signal Forecast Snapshot — biweekly
content:
Purpose:
A compact biweekly snapshot covering onboarding eval signals, promptset health, and a prioritized action plan. This doc is intended for applied-ml leads and SRE/product partners who need a concise, operational view and clear next steps.

Executive summary (TL;DR):
- Aggregate quality score across 14 days dropped 3.6 points (from 88.1 -> 84.5). Decline concentrated in two customer prompt bundles (commerce-rewrite, form-summarize).
- Top emerging failure mode: hallucinated pricing details when partial price context provided (observed in 18% of commerce-rewrite failures).
- Promptset health index: commerce-rewrite = 0.58, form-summarize = 0.63 (scale 0–1, 1=healthy).
- Primary short-term mitigations: soft fallback to smaller-context variant (deploy by 2026-08-02), targeted prompt anchors for price entities, and a promptset curation sweep.

Key metrics (14-day window ending 2026-07-29):
- Total eval runs: 12,320
- Signal coverage (unique promptsets contributing >= 20 requests): 42
- Aggregate quality score (weighted): 84.5
- False-positives (hallucinated facts): 7.2% (up from 4.1%)
- Rejection / safety-trigger rate: 0.9% (stable)
- Average tail latency (95p): 310ms (+20ms)

Signal attribution and heatmap notes:
- Commerce-rewrite bundle contributed 36% of total failures; within that bundle, 60% were price hallucinations, 25% were unit/quantity confusion, 15% formatting/markdown bugs.
- Form-summarize bundle shows an increase in omitted critical fields (phone/email) at a rate of +4pp. Root suspect: recent prompt edit that removed explicit "include contact fields" anchor (see linked PR).
- New customer signal (acct: bluebay) shows pattern of extremely long context with many HTML artifacts. We see elevated token truncation errors causing hallucinations.

Failure taxonomy (why these failures matter):
1) Fact hallucination — incorrect price, discounts fabricated. Business impact: high for commerce customers (revenue/KPIs).
2) Context truncation — dropped antecedents from long HTML forms resulting in incomplete outputs. Impacts downstream parsers.
3) Entity normalization — inconsistent unit handling (lbs vs kg) leading to wrong interpretations.
4) Format regression — previously working markdown framing now inconsistent across model roll.

Root-cause hypotheses (ranked):
- H1: Recent model variant rollout (v3.2.1-q8b) uses a decoding temperature/penalty config that slightly increases creative completions. Evidence: timing correlation with rollout on 2026-07-18 and jump in hallucination signals.
- H2: Prompt edits in commerce-rewrite (frontend PR #512) inadvertently removed explicit negative examples for fabricated prices.
- H3: Inadequate prompt anchors for long-HTML contexts; KV cache eviction patterns for long sequences cause missing tokens at critical positions.

Promptset health and remediation suggestions: 
- Commerce-rewrite (health 0.58): curate 30 new negative examples, add explicit anchor "do not invent prices", and add a quick post-checker that verifies price formats against provided context. Owner: Marcus Lee. ETA: 2026-08-04.
- Form-summarize (health 0.63): re-add contact-field anchor, add 150-shot synthetic edge examples with truncated HTML. Owner: Sana Patel. ETA: 2026-08-06.
- Bluebay customer: create a preprocessor that strips noisy HTML and normalizes tokens before sending to model. Owner: Evan Park. ETA: 2026-08-03.

Top failures (examples and prevalence):
- Price hallucination in commerce-rewrite: 1,092 incidents (18% of that bundle's fails). Example: "Total after discount: $49.99" when invoice context shows $0 or no price.
- Omitted contact fields in form-summarize: 432 incidents. Example: Summary omits phone number present in form body.
- Unit mismatch: 210 incidents where "5 lbs" was interpreted as "5 kg" in shipping advice outputs.

Immediate mitigations (fast-fail safe changes):
- Deploy prompt prefix variants that include a strict "do not invent" guardrail for commerce-rewrite to 25% of traffic (canary). Risk: minor latency cost due to additional post-check. Owner: Riley Chen. Due: 2026-08-02.
- Add a deterministic post-output sanity check for price fields that rejects outputs without any price token when input contains price-like tokens. Implement as sidecar validation. Owner: Marcus Lee. Due: 2026-08-01.

Longer-term work (owner, priority, ETA):
- Revisit decoding hyperparams for v3.2.x family and run an A/B sweep vs v3.1.x baseline for hallucination rate (Priority: P0). Owner: Applied ML infra (Evan Park). ETA: 2026-08-14.
- Expand promptset regression suite with synthetic HTML-noise cases (P1). Owner: Sana Patel. ETA: 2026-08-10.
- KV-cache diagnostics: instrument eviction rate vs failure correlation (P1). Owner: Platform-engineering (Riley Chen). ETA: 2026-08-09.

Action items (owners and status):
- [In progress] Marcus Lee — price post-check sidecar prototype (branch: price-guard-proto). Target 2026-08-01.
- [To do] Sana Patel — prompt anchor rework for form-summarize; coordinate with QA for 150-shot examples. Target 2026-08-06.
- [In progress] Evan Park — preprocess HTML stripper for bluebay canary tests. Target 2026-08-03.
- [To do] Riley Chen — configure canary routing for guarded prompt prefix (25% traffic). Target 2026-08-02.
- [Blocked] Product PM (J. Morales) — decision on rollback vs hyperparam adjustment for v3.2.1-q8b. Blockers: risk review and stakeholder sign-off. 

Monitoring and observability updates required:
- Add a dedicated metric for "price-mismatch rate" to the onboarding dashboard (tile + alert at 2% absolute increase).
- Create an SLO runbook for hallucination surges: paging thresholds, initial responder, and if/when to auto-fallback to baseline model.
- Add per-promptset tagging to traces so we can quickly filter regressions to upstream prompt edits.

Communications plan:
- Notify customer success for affected customers (commerce vertical) by 2026-08-01 with mitigations and ETA. Owner: Customer Success lead.
- Weekly sync with product and SRE on mitigation progress every Tuesday 10:30am PST starting 2026-08-04.

Open questions / decision points:
- Rollback vs hyperparam tweak for v3.2.1-q8b: is a rollback acceptable from a capacity/contract standpoint? (need input from infra and sales).
- Do we enforce stricter prompt-change reviews (mandatory negative-case examples) for production promptsets? Cost: slower PR flow.

Appendix (quick links and traces):
- Example failing trace: github.com/redwood-inference/traces/trace-5543
- Related GH PRs: github.com/redwood-inference/ui/pull/512 (commerce prompt change)
- Relevant Jira: JIRA-EVAL-721 (commerce hallucination spike), JIRA-OPS-808 (canary routing), JIRA-PLAT-617 (KV eviction diag)

Notes and context for reviewers:
- This doc is deliberately short and operational; the goal is to converge on 2 quick mitigations (post-checker + guardrail prompt) and an instrumentation spike to verify the hyperparam hypothesis. Please flag if any owner is unavailable or if this should escalate to exec review.

Prepared by: Aisha Kapoor (applied-ml)
Reviewers: Marcus Lee, Sana Patel, Evan Park, Riley Chen
